title: Johor OSAT Expansion: New Facilities and Lead Times
abstract: Our insider just got back from Johor with a notebook full of numbers that will make your capacity planning cry.
body:
## The Johor OSAT Boom Nobody Priced In

I spent 2026-04-28 to 2026-05-01 on the ground in Johor, and I came back with a notebook that should scare every fabless planner who still thinks assembly and test is a buyer's market. The Malaysians are building out OSAT capacity at a clip I have not seen since Penang in 2021, but the lead times are not shrinking. They are stretching. As of 2026-05-05, my best intel says new wire bond and flip chip lines in Johor will not be qualified for volume production until Q1 2027 at the earliest. That is 34 weeks from today if you are counting, and you should be.

## What Is Actually Being Built

Three major OSAT players have broken ground in the Johor Bahru tech corridor since late 2025. The first is a 120,000 square foot facility focused on advanced packaging for automotive MCUs. The second is a 200,000 square foot plant that will do wafer-level packaging and test for RF front-end modules. The third is a retrofit of an existing building into a 90,000 square foot line for memory and logic test. Combined, that is roughly 410,000 square feet of new cleanroom space. Sounds like a lot until you realize that TSMC alone consumes more than that in a single quarter for its advanced packaging needs. So Johor is not solving the global shortage. It is solving a regional gap for Southeast Asian fabless firms that are tired of paying Singapore prices.

I talked to a procurement director at one of the OSATs. He would not give me exact numbers, but he did say that their equipment lead times for die bonders and wire bonders are running 28 to 36 weeks. That is up from 16 weeks in 2024. The bottleneck is not the building. It is the back-end tools. And those tools are made by a handful of vendors who are already maxed out serving TSMC and Intel. So Johor gets the scraps. That means your 2026 ramp plans are already dead if you were counting on Johor capacity.

## Lead Times by Package Type

Here is what I am hearing from three different sources as of 2026-05-05. For QFN and other leadframe packages, new capacity in Johor will be ready for production samples in 18 weeks. That puts you at early September 2026. For volume, add another 12 weeks. So February 2027. For flip chip ball grid array, the story is worse. The new lines need 26 weeks for sample qualification and another 16 weeks for volume. That is 42 weeks total, which lands you in late February 2027. For wafer-level chip scale packages, the RF line I mentioned is targeting 30 weeks to sample and 20 weeks to volume. That is 50 weeks, or mid-April 2027. And for system-in-package modules, forget it. The OSATs are not even quoting new programs until Q3 2026 because they are still debugging the first wave.

Compare that to what you can get in Taiwan or South Korea today. A mature QFN line in Hsinchu can turn samples in 8 weeks and volume in 16. Flip chip in Korea is 14 weeks to sample and 28 to volume. So Johor is not competitive on speed. It is competitive on cost. Labor is 40 percent cheaper than Singapore, and the Malaysian government is handing out tax holidays like candy. But cheap does not help you if you miss your window.

## The BoJ Factor

Here is the part that nobody in Johor wants to talk about. The Bank of Japan meets on 2026-06-16, and the yen is already at 158 to the dollar. If the BoJ hikes rates again, the yen could strengthen to 145. That would make Japanese OSAT capacity more expensive relative to Malaysian ringgit. But it would also make Japanese equipment cheaper for everyone else. The die bonders and wire bonders I mentioned? Most of them are made in Japan. A stronger yen means those tools get more expensive for Malaysian OSATs, which means they delay orders, which means your lead times stretch even further. I have seen this movie before in 2022. It did not end well for anyone who was long on optimism.

My advice is simple. If you have a program that needs Johor capacity in 2026, kill it now. If you need it in 2027, start negotiating today and expect to pay a premium for priority. And if you are still relying on spot market capacity for your Q3 2026 build, you are already too late. The OSATs in Johor are not your savior. They are a 12 to 18 month project that will help you in 2028. Plan accordingly.

## What I Am Watching Next

Two things. First, the equipment move-in schedules for the three Johor facilities. I have heard that the first die bonders will arrive in week 24 of 2026, which is mid-June. If that slips by even four weeks, push your volume dates out by eight weeks. Second, the Malaysian government's next round of tax incentives, which is expected in the 2027 budget. If they extend the tax holiday for another five years, you will see a fourth OSAT announce a Johor facility by Q4 2026. That would be good news for 2028 capacity, but it does nothing for your 2026 and 2027 pain. I will be back in Johor in August. Until then, assume the worst and you will not be far off.
